integrator_questions: Does the signal stay stable with the row at 80 mm, or does the extra lag need more kd to damp the response on the s-bend and slalom?
Where does max_error occur now, at bend entry (lag) or during recovery (overshoot)? Compare with iteration 0 at 60 mm.
Does line_loss_events change with the longer lookahead, given the sensors now see the line before the robot reaches it?

intent: Test the lookahead trend in isolation. Keep the iteration 0 baseline (0.8 kg, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.12 m body width, 12 mm sensors on a 12 mm pitch) and move only the sensor row from y = 0.06 m to y = 0.08 m, the upper bound. The 40 mm, 60 mm and 80 mm rows give a monotone test: if 80 mm beats 60 mm, longer lookahead is the lever; if it falls back, the optimum lies near 60 mm and the next variable is wheel track or sensor pitch.
learning: Iterations 0 to 2 show a monotone trend: lookahead 40 mm scored 52.25, 60 mm scored 65.96 (best), with iteration 1 confounded. The working hypothesis is that longer lookahead improves anticipation on bends, so the 80 mm test should improve on 60 mm if the trend holds. If it does not, the lookahead optimum is near 60 mm, and the next single-variable tests are wheel_track (turn authority) and sensor pitch (resolution on tight bends).
rationale: Iteration 2 moved the sensor row from 60 mm to 40 mm ahead of the axle, with everything else as in iteration 0. The score fell from 65.96 to 52.25. Oval progress dropped from 0.20 to 0.11, s-bend progress from 0.16 to 0.16 with more line loss, and max_error stayed at 0.06 to 0.065 on every track. Shorter lookahead therefore made things worse, which contradicts the lag hypothesis I had for iteration 2. The cleanest reading is that the controller benefits from seeing the line further ahead, so less lookahead means less anticipation and more overshoot. Iteration 1 also reduced oval progress when mass, track, sensor size and pitch changed together, so I will not combine changes again. The next single-variable step along the observed trend is to move the sensor row to the maximum allowed forward position, 80 mm ahead of the axle, and hold every other value at the iteration 0 baseline. I expect max_error to fall below or near the 0.06 m off-track limit, progress to rise on the oval and slalom, and the score to beat 66. The risk is that extra lag at the 80 mm limit cancels the benefit, which would show as higher steering oscillation.
